semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {مِنَ الرهب}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to one of four things: either to «ولى», or to «مُدْبِراً», or to «اضْمُمْ» — this third becomes apparent if we explain الرَّهْب as "the sleeve" — or to something omitted, i.e. "[be calm] from الرَّهْب". Ḥafṣ read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ; the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr with ḍamma and sukūn; the rest with two fatḥas; al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā, al-Jaḥdarī and Qatāda with two ḍammas. All of them are dialectal forms meaning "fear". It has been said: with two fatḥas it is "the sleeve" in the dialect of Ḥimyar and Ḥanīfa. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is one of the novelties of exegesis." He said: "Would that I knew how sound it is in the language, and whether it has been heard from the reliable, trustworthy authorities whose Arabic is accepted! And would that I knew what its place is in the verse and how it is applied in detail like the rest of the words of the Revelation — given that Moses, Allah's blessings be upon him, on the night of the intimate converse had on him nothing but a رُزْمانِقَة of wool with no sleeves." The رُزْمانِقَة is the مِدْرَعَة (a woollen tunic).
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is narrated from al-Aṣmaʿī, and he is reliable; he heard them say: أَعْطِني ما في رَهْبِك, i.e. 'in your sleeve'. As for his saying 'what is its place?', they said: its meaning is 'take your hand out of your sleeve'." I say: how can this explanation be sound? They explain اضْمُمْ as meaning "take out"!
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the wing — which is the hand — has been made in one of the two places the thing drawn in, and in the other the thing drawn to, namely His saying {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ} and His saying {واضمم يَدَكَ إلى جَنَاحِكَ}; so how are they reconciled? I say: what is meant by the wing that is drawn in is the right hand, and by the wing drawn to is the left hand, and each one of the right and left hands is a wing."
His saying: {فَذَانِكَ}: the reading with a light and a doubled [nūn] has already been treated in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. Ibn Masʿūd, ʿĪsā, Shibl and Abū Nawfal read it with a yāʾ after a nūn with kasra [فذانيك], and this is the dialect of Hudhayl; it has also been said: of Tamīm. Shibl narrated from Ibn Kathīr a yāʾ after a nūn with fatḥa; this follows the dialect of those who give the dual nūn a fatḥa, as in his saying:
3604 - على أَحْوَذِيَّيْنَ اسْتَقلَّتْ عَشِيَّةً ... فما هي إلاَّ لَمْحَةٌ وتَغيبُ
(She rose one evening upon two swift wings, and it was but a glance and she was gone.)
And the yāʾ is a substitute for one of the two nūns, as in «تَظَنَّيْت». ʿAbdallāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read it with a doubled nūn followed by a yāʾ, and it has been ascribed to Hudhayl. Al-Mahdawī said: rather, their dialect is with the light form. And I do not think the kasra here is anything other than an extension (ishbāʿ), like the reading of Hishām {أَفْئِيدَةً مِّنَ الناس} [Ibrāhīm: 37].
And «ذانِكَ» points to the staff and the hand, both of which are feminine; what points to them was only made masculine because of the masculinity of their khabar (predicate), which is «برهانان», just as it is sometimes made feminine because of the femininity of its khabar, as in the reading {ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} [al-Anʿām: 23] by those who read it feminine and put «فِتْنَتَهم» in the accusative, and likewise the poet's saying:
3605 - . . . . . . . . . . ... فقد خابَ مَنْ كانَتْ سَرِيْرَتَه الغَدْرُ
(…then he has failed whose inner secret was treachery.)
The explanation of this has preceded in al-Anʿām. The derivation of البُرْهان has also preceded.
Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: why is a proof called بُرْهان? I say: because of its whiteness and radiance, from their calling a white woman بَرَهْرَهَة, with repetition of the ʿayn and lām [radicals]. The proof that the nūn is additional is their saying أَبْرَهَ الرجلُ when he brings a بُرْهان. Similar to it is their calling it سُلْطان, from السَّليط, which is oil, because of its radiance."
His saying: {إلى فِرْعَوْنَ}: it is attached to something omitted; Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as "sent to Pharaoh", and others as "go to Pharaoh". This implied element ought to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «برهانان», i.e. "sent with them to Pharaoh", and the governor of this ḥāl is the [verbal sense] contained in the demonstrative.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {هُوَ أَفْصَحُ}: الفَصاحَة lexically is purity. From it: فَصُحَ اللبنُ and أَفْصَحَ, so it is مُفْصِح and فَصيح, i.e. it has become clear of the froth. Their saying is narrated:
3606 - . . . . . . . . . . ... وتحتَ الرَّغْوَةِ اللبنُ الفَصيحُ
(…and beneath the froth is the pure milk.)
From it: فَصُحَ الرجل: his language became excellent; and أَفْصَحَ: he spoke Arabic. It has also been said: the reverse. It has been said: the فصيح is the one who speaks and the أعجم is the one who does not speak. From this was borrowed أَفْصَحَ الصبحُ, i.e. its light appeared; and أفصح النصرانيُّ: his فِصْح drew near — with kasra on the fāʾ — which is a feast of theirs. As for the technical usage of the scholars of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān), it is the word's freedom from dissonance of letters, as in his saying «ترعى الهِعْخِع»; from strangeness, as in his saying:
3607 - . . . . . . . . . . ومَرْسِناً مُسَرَّجاً ...
(…and a nose [shaped] like a polished sword [or: a lamp].)
and from contravening lexical analogy, as in his saying:
3608 - . . . . . . . . . . العَليِّ الأَجْلَل ...
(…the Most High, the Most Majestic [with the unassimilated form الأجلل].)
And the speech's freedom from weak composition, as in his saying:
3609 - جزى ربُّه عني عَدِيَّ بنَ حاتمٍ ... . . . . . . . . . .
(May his Lord reward ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim on my behalf… [the pronoun precedes its referent].)
and from dissonance of words, as in his saying:
3610 - وقبرُ حربٍ بمكانٍ قَفْرِ ... وليسَ قربَ قبرِ حَرْبٍ قبرُ
(The grave of Ḥarb is in a desolate place, and there is no grave near the grave of Ḥarb.)
and from complexity (taʿqīd), which is either a disruption of the arrangement of the speech so that it is not known how to reach its meaning, as in his saying:
3611 - وما مثلُه في الناسِ إلاَّ مُمَلَّكاً ... أبو أمِّه حيٌّ أبوه يُقارِبُهْ
(There is none like him among people, alive, who approaches him, except a king whose mother's father is his [the praised man's] father.)
or the mind's failure to pass from the first meaning to the second meaning — which is its concomitant and what is intended by it — in an apparent way, as in his saying:
3612 - سأطلبُ بُعْدَ الدارِ عنكم لِتَقْرَبُوا ... وَتَسْكُبُ عينايَ الدموعَ لتَجْمُدا
(I shall seek to be far from you so that you may come near, and my eyes shall pour tears so that they may become dry.)
And the speaker's freedom from uttering any of that. So faṣāḥa is attributed to three things: the word, the speech and the speaker — unlike balāgha (eloquence), with which only the last two are described. This has a place where it is explained; I have only mentioned to you what alerts you to its basis.
And [his saying] «لِساناً» is a tamyīz (specification).
His saying: «رِدْءاً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). الرِّدْء is the helper; it is of the pattern فِعْل in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), like الدِّفْء in the sense of "that by which one is warmed". رَدَأْتُه على عَدُوِّه: I helped him against his enemy. رَدَأْتُ الحائط: I propped the wall with a beam so that it would not fall. Al-Naḥḥās said: "One says رَدَأْته and أَرْدَأْته."
Salāma ibn Jandal said:
3613 - ورِدْئي كلُّ أبيضَ مَشْرَفيٍّ ... شَحيذِ الحَدِّ أبيضَ ذي فُلولِ
(My helper is every gleaming Mashrafī sword, sharp of edge, gleaming, with notches.)
Another said:
3614 - ألم تَرَ أنَّ أَصْرَمَ كان رِدْئي ... وخيرَ الناسِ في قُلٍّ ومالِ
(Have you not seen that Aṣram was my helper, and the best of people in poverty and wealth?)
Nāfiʿ read «رِدا» with transfer [of the hamza's vowel], and Abū Jaʿfar likewise except that he did not give it tanwīn, as though he treated the continuation like the pause. Nāfiʿ's rule does not include transfer within a single word except here. It has been said: there is no transfer in it; rather it is from أردى على كذا, i.e. "exceeded". The poet said:
3615 - وأسمرَ خَطِّيّاً كأنَّ كُعُوبَه ... نوى القَسْبِ قد أردى ذِراعاً على العَشْرِ
(And a tawny Khaṭṭī spear whose knots are like the stones of dry dates, that has exceeded ten [cubits] by a cubit.)
i.e. exceeded. [Al-Jawharī recited it as قد أربى, which has the same meaning.]
His saying: {يُصَدِّقُنِي}: Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read it in the nominative, as resumptive, or as a naʿt (adjective) of «رِدْءاً», or as a ḥāl from the hāʾ of «أَرْسِلْه», or from the pronoun in «رِدْءاً». The rest read it in the jussive as the answer to the imperative. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ubayy read «يُصَدِّقوني», i.e. Pharaoh and his chiefs. Ibn Khālawayh said: "This is evidence for those who read the jussive, because had it been nominative he would have said «يُصَدِّقونَني»," meaning with two nūns.
This is an oversight on Ibn Khālawayh's part, because whenever the nūn of the nominative meets the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), several options are permitted, one of them being deletion; so this may be nominative, its nūn deleted for the reason I have mentioned to you. The verification of this has preceded in al-Anʿām and elsewhere. The Shaykh reported it from Ibn Khālawayh and did not follow it with any objection.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {عَضُدَكَ}: the generality read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the ḍād. Al-Ḥasan and Zayd ibn ʿAlī with ḍamma on both; from al-Ḥasan also a ḍamma and a sukūn; ʿĪsā with fatḥa on both; and some with fatḥa on the ʿayn and kasra on the ḍād. There is a sixth dialectal form: fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn on the ḍād, which I do not know as a reading. This is a metonymy for strengthening him through his brother.
His saying: {بِآيَاتِنَآ}: several views are possible in it: that it is attached to «نَجْعَلُ», or to «يَصِلُوْن», or to something omitted, i.e. "go [both of you]", or it is for clarification (bayān) and so also attached to something omitted, or to «الغالبون» — on the view that the al is not a relative, or that it is a relative but latitude is allowed in it [i.e. in the adverbial] that is not allowed elsewhere — or it is an oath whose answer precedes it, namely «فلا يَصِلُون», or it is of the void oath (laghw al-qasam). Al-Zamakhsharī said these last two. The Shaykh refuted him on the grounds that the fāʾ does not enter the answer of an oath according to the majority. By the void oath he means that its answer is omitted, i.e. "By the truth of Our signs, you will surely prevail."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {وَقَالَ موسى}: this is the reading of the generality, with the conjunctive wāw retained. Ibn Kathīr omitted it, and each agrees with his codex, for it is present in the codices except the codex of Mecca. Its retention and its omission are both clear; it is what the scholars of rhetoric call conjunction and disjunction (al-waṣl wa-l-faṣl).
His saying: {وَمَن تَكُونُ}: the generality read «تكون» in the feminine, with «له» its khabar (predicate) and «عاقبةُ» its noun. It is possible that its noun is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), the feminine being for that reason, and {لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ الدار} a clause in the position of the khabar. It was also read with the lower-dotted yāʾ [يكون], on the view that «عاقبةٌ» is its noun and the masculine is because of the separation, since the femininity is metaphorical. It is possible that its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause a khabar as preceded. It is possible that it is complete (tāmma), containing a pronoun referring back to «مَنْ», the clause being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). And it is possible that it is incomplete (nāqiṣa), its noun being the pronoun of «مَنْ» and the clause its khabar.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {بِغَيْرِ الحق}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they were arrogant, being involved in what is other than the truth.
His saying: {لاَ يُرْجَعُونَ}: Nāfiʿ and the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it in the active voice, and the rest in the passive.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ}, i.e. We made them [into]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "We called them", as though he fled from attributing that — I mean the making — to Allah the Exalted, because it does not agree with his doctrine. And «يَدْعُون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أَئمةً».
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ}: there are several views in it. The first: that it is attached to «المقبوحين», on the view that the al is not a relative, or that it is a relative and latitude is allowed in it. [The second:] that it is attached to something omitted which «المقبوحين» explains, as though it were said "and they will be made wretched on the Day of Resurrection", like {لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِّنَ القالين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 168]. Or that it is conjoined to the position of «في الدنيا», i.e. "and We made a curse follow them on the Day of Resurrection". Or that it is conjoined to «لعنةً» with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "and the curse of the Day of Resurrection". The second view is the most apparent of them.
المقبوح is the one driven away. قبَّحه الله: [Allah] drove him away. He said:
3616 - ألا قَبَّح اللهُ البراجِمَ كلِّها ... وجَدَّعَ يَرْبُوعاً وعَقَّر دارِما
(May Allah make wretched the Barājim, all of them, and mutilate Yarbūʿ and hamstring Dārim!)
The opposite of beauty was called قبيح because the eye shrinks from it, as though it drives it away. One says قَبُح قَباحةً. It has also been said: «من المقبوحين» means of those marked with a detestable sign, such as blueness of the eyes and blackness of the faces. القبيح is also the bone of the forearm, from its middle to the elbow.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {بَصَآئِرَ}: it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a ḥāl (circumstantial): either with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "possessing insights", or by way of hyperbole.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {بِجَانِبِ الغربي}: it may be of the omission of the qualified noun and the setting up of its adjective in its place, i.e. "at the side of the western place"; or it may be of the annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective, which is the doctrine of the Kufans. Like it: «بَقْلةُ الحمقَاء» and «مَسْجد الجامع».

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {وَلَكِنَّآ أَنشَأْنَا}: the point of the rectification (istidrāk) is that the meaning is: "you were not a witness for Moses of what befell him, but We revealed it to you." So He mentioned the cause of the revelation, which is the lengthening of the interval [between prophets], and indicated by it the effect, in keeping with Allah the Exalted's custom in His concise expressions. So this rectification resembles the two rectifications after it. Al-Zamakhsharī said this after a long discussion.
His saying: {ثَاوِياً}, i.e. residing. One says ثوى يَثْوِي ثَواءً وثَوِيّاً, and he is ثاوٍ and مَثْوِيّ. Dhū al-Rumma said:
3617 - لقد كانَ في حَوْلٍ ثَواءٍ ثوَيْتُه ... تَقَضِّي لُباناتٍ ويُسْأَمُ سائِمُ
(In a year of staying that I stayed there was the fulfilment of desires, and the one who wearies grows weary.)
Another said:
3618 - طال الثَّواءُ على رُسومِ المنزلِ ... . . . . . . . . . .
(Long has been the staying at the traces of the dwelling…)
Al-ʿAjjāj said:
3619 - فباتَ حيث يَدْخُلُ الثَّوِيُّ ...
(So he spent the night where the resident guest enters.)
meaning the resident guest.
His saying: {تَتْلُواْ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «ثاويا», or a second khabar (predicate), or it may be the khabar with «ثاوياً» a ḥāl. Al-Farrāʾ made it cut off from what precedes it, i.e. resumptive, as though it were said: "and here you are reciting to your community". There is remoteness in that.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {مَّآ أَتَاهُم مِّن نَّذِيرٍ}: it is in the position of an adjective (ṣifa) of «قوماً».
[His saying:] {ولكن رَّحْمَةً}, i.e. "We sent you as a mercy" or "We informed you of that as a mercy". ʿĪsā and Abū Ḥaywa read it in the nominative, i.e. "you are a mercy".

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {ولولا أَن تُصِيبَهُم}: it is the lawlā of impossibility (imtināʿiyya). أنْ and what falls within its scope is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "were it not for the calamity's befalling them". Its answer is omitted; al-Zajjāj estimated it as "We would not have sent messengers to them", meaning that what prompted sending the messengers was the removal of their excuses with this saying, so it is like His saying {لِئَلاَّ يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى الله حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرسل} [al-Nisāʾ: 165]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated it as "We would have hastened [punishment] upon them", and this has no meaning.
And «فَيَقولوا» is conjoined [to] «تُصيبَهم»; the second «لولا» is of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and «فنَتَّبِعَ» is its answer, which is why it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is this meaning sound when the punishment has been made the cause, not the saying, since the particle of impossibility enters upon it and not upon the saying? I say: the saying is what is intended to be the cause of the sending; but since the punishment was the cause of the saying, and the saying exists by its existence, the punishment was made as though it were a cause of the sending by means of the saying, so «لولا» was made to enter upon it, and the saying was brought conjoined to it with the fāʾ that gives the sense of causation. Its meaning reduces to your saying: 'Were it not for their saying this when a calamity befalls them, We would not have sent [messengers].' But this route was chosen for a subtle point: namely that had they not been punished, for example, for their disbelief — having witnessed that by which they were compelled to certain knowledge — they would not have said 'Why did You not send us a messenger?'; the cause of their saying this is the punishment and nothing else, not regret over the faith in their Creator that they missed."

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: it is attached either to «يكفروا» or to «أُوْتِي», i.e. "before your appearance".
His saying: {سِحْرَانِ}: the Kufans read «سِحْران», i.e. "they are [two sorceries]", meaning the Qurʾān and the Torah, or Moses and Aaron — this by way of hyperbole, making them sorcery itself — or with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "possessors of two sorceries". If this were sound, «سِحْر» ought to have been singular, but it was put in the dual to draw attention to the [two] kinds. It has been said: what is meant is Moses and Muḥammad, peace be upon them both, or the Torah and the Gospel. The rest read «ساحران», i.e. Moses and Aaron, or Moses and Muḥammad, as preceded.
His saying: {تَظَاهَرَا}: the generality read it with a light ẓāʾ, as a past verb, an adjective (ṣifa) of «سِحْران» or «ساحران», i.e. "they supported each other". Al-Ḥasan, Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith al-Dhimārī, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Yazīdī read it with the ẓāʾ doubled, and people have declared them to be in error. Ibn Khālawayh said: "Doubling it is an error, because it is a past verb, and doubling only occurs in the imperfect." Al-Hudhalī said: "It has no meaning." Abū al-Faḍl said: "I do not know its rationale." This is astonishing from these [scholars], when the nūn of the nominative has been deleted in places, even in eloquent speech, as in his saying, peace be upon him: «لا تَدْخلوا الجنةَ حتى تؤْمِنوا ولا تُؤْمنوا حتى تحابُّوا» ("You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another"). There is no difference between its coming after a wāw, an alif or a yāʾ. So the original of this is «تَتَظاهران»; it was assimilated, and its nūn deleted for lightness.
Al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa read — and so it is in the codex of ʿAbdallāh — «اظَّاهَرا», with a connective hamza and a doubled ẓāʾ. Its original is «تَظاهرا», as in the reading of the generality; when assimilation was intended, you made the first [letter] quiescent, and so the connective hamza was brought in.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {أَتَّبِعْهُ}: it is the answer to the imperative, which is «فَأْتوا». «منهما», i.e. from the Torah and the Qurʾān — and this supports the reading «سِحْران» — or from their two books, with a muḍāf omitted — and this supports the reading «ساحِران». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أتَّبِعُه» in the nominative, as resumptive, i.e. "for I will follow it".

semin-durr:50-50.t:
[His saying]: {فَإِن لَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ لَكَ}: استجاب means أجاب (to answer). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the difference between the verb of responding in the verse and in his saying:
3620 - . . . . . . . . . . ... فلم يَسْتَجِبْه عند ذاك مُجِيْبُ
(…and no answerer answered him at that time.)
where it is made transitive without a lām? I say: this verb is transitive to the supplication by itself and to the supplicant by means of the lām; and the supplication is usually omitted when it is made transitive to the supplicant, so one says 'Allah answered his supplication' or 'answered him', and one hardly says 'answered him his supplication'. As for the verse, its meaning is 'did not answer his supplication', with the muḍāf omitted." I say: the establishment of this has preceded in al-Baqara, and that استجاب means أجاب. The verse to which he alluded is:
وداعٍ دَعا يا مَنْ يُجيب إلى الندى ... فلم يَسْتَجِبْه عند ذاك مُجيبُ
(Many a caller has called, "O who will answer [the call] to generosity?", and no answerer answered him at that time.)

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {وَصَّلْنَا}: the generality read it with doubling, either from الوصل, the opposite of cutting, i.e. "We made parts of it follow other parts" — its origin is from the joining of a rope; the poet said:
3621 - فَقُلْ لبني مروانَ ما بالُ ذِمَّتي ... بحبلٍ ضعيفِ لا يَزال يُوَصَّل
(Say to the sons of Marwān: what is the matter with my covenant [being tied] by a weak rope that is constantly being spliced?)
— or "We made it into joints", i.e. kinds of meanings; Mujāhid said this. Al-Ḥasan read it with a light ṣād, and it is close to what preceded.

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {الذين آتَيْنَاهُمُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); «هم» is a second mubtadaʾ and «يؤْمِنون» its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of the first, and «به» is attached to «يُؤْمِنون». This may cause difficulty for al-Zamakhsharī and other scholars of rhetoric, since they said that fronting conveys restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ), and that cannot be the case here, because had they restricted their faith to this Book alone, their disbelief in what is besides it would follow, which is the opposite of what is intended. The scholars of rhetoric raised this in His saying {آمَنَّا بِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا} [al-Mulk: 29], saying: had «به» been fronted, it would have suggested restriction of faith to Allah alone, excluding His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day; and this very thing applies here. The answer is that faith in other than it is known, so the purpose was directed to faith in this.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {مَّرَّتَيْنِ}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). In {بِمَا صَبَرُواْ}, «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the bāʾ is attached to «يُؤْتَوْن» or to «الأجر» itself.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying: {نُتَخَطَّفْ}: the generality read it in the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). Al-Minqarī read it in the nominative, with the fāʾ omitted, as in his saying:
3622 - مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يَشْكرها ... . . . . . . . . . .
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will appreciate them…)
and like the reading of «يُدْرِكُكُمْ» [al-Nisāʾ: 78] in the nominative; or on the basis of fronting [i.e. it is in intention placed before the condition], which is the doctrine of Sībawayh.
His saying: {أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَماً}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He made it transitive by itself because it has the meaning of جَعَلَ, and He has stated it explicitly in His saying {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَماً} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 67]." [But] مَكَّن is transitive by itself without being made to contain the meaning of جَعَلَ, as in His saying {مَكَّنَّاهم}. Its verification has preceded in al-Anʿām.
And «آمِناً»: it has been said it means مُؤَمَّن, i.e. whoever enters it is granted security. It has been said: it is with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "its people being secure". And it has been said: it is the pattern فاعِل in the sense of relation, i.e. "possessing security".
His saying: {يجبى}: Nāfiʿ read it with the feminine tāʾ, in regard to the wording of «ثَمَرات»; the rest with the yāʾ because of the separation and because the femininity is metaphorical. The clause is also an adjective (ṣifa) of «حرماً». The generality read «ثَمَرات» with two fatḥas; Abān with two ḍammas, the plural of ثُمُر with two ḍammas; and some with a fatḥa and a sukūn.
His saying: «رِزْقاً»: if you make it a maṣdar (verbal noun), it may be accusative as an emphatic maṣdar, because the meaning of «يجبى إليه» is "He provides for them"; or accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the governor being omitted, i.e. "We drive it to it as provision"; or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ثَمَرات», since it is specified by the annexation. If you make it a noun for what is provided, it is accusative as a ḥāl from «ثَمَرات».

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {مَعِيشَتَهَا}: there are several views in it: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by making بَطِرَتْ contain the meaning of خَسِرَت ("lost"); or as an adverbial, i.e. "the days of its livelihood" — al-Zajjāj said this; or by omission of «في», i.e. "in its livelihood"; or as a tamyīz (specification); or by resemblance to the direct object, which is close to {سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ} [al-Baqara: 130].
His saying: {لَمْ تُسْكَن}: a circumstantial clause, its governor being the meaning of «تلك». It may also be a second khabar (predicate).
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}, i.e. except a little dwelling, like the dwelling of a traveller and the like; or except a little time; or except a little place — meaning that a small part of them has been dwelt in.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {فَمَتَاعُ}, i.e. "then it is the enjoyment". It was also read «فمتاعاً الحياةَ», with «متاعاً» accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they enjoy an enjoyment", and «الحياةَ» accusative as an adverbial.
His saying: {تَعْقِلُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr read it with the lower-dotted yāʾ, by way of shift of address (iltifāt); the rest in the second person, continuing what preceded.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
Ṭalḥa read «أمَنْ وَعَدْناه» without the fāʾ.
His saying: {ثُمَّ هُوَ}: al-Kisāʾī and Qālūn [read it] with a sukūn on the hāʾ, treating ثم like the wāw and the fāʾ; the rest with a ḍamma, according to the original.

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {الذين كُنتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ}: its two objects are omitted, i.e. "you claimed them to be partners".

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {هؤلاء الذين أَغْوَيْنَآ}: there are two views in it. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «الذين أَغْوَيْنا» an adjective of the mubtadaʾ, the referent pronoun omitted, i.e. "whom we led astray", and the khabar (predicate) is «أَغْوَيْناهم»; and {كَمَا غَوَيْنَا} is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that maṣdar being the reflexive counterpart (muṭāwiʿ) of this verb, i.e. "[we led them astray] and they went astray as we went astray". Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Abū ʿAlī rejected this view, saying: "Because there is no additional information in the khabar beyond what is in its adjective." He said: "If you say: it has been joined to His saying {كَمَا غَوَيْنَا}, and there is an addition in it, I say: the addition in an adverbial does not make it a principal part of the clause, because adverbials are adjuncts." Then he himself parsed «هؤلاء» as a mubtadaʾ and «الذين أَغْوَيْناهم» as its khabar, with «أَغْوَيْناهم» resumptive. [Translator's note: the text here reads «الذين أَغْوَيْناهم» with the pronoun, where the verse reads «الذين أَغْوَيْنا»; translated as written.] Abū al-Baqāʾ and others answered the first [objection] that an adverbial is sometimes indispensable, as in your saying «زيد عمرٌو في دارِه» ("Zayd — ʿAmr is in his house").
His saying: {مَا كانوا إِيَّانَا يَعْبُدُونَ}: «إيَّانا» is the object of «يَعْبُدون», fronted for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila). In «ما» there are two views. The first: it is negating. The second: it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), in which case a preposition must be assumed, i.e. "we disown what they used to [do]", i.e. "their worship of us". There is remoteness in this.

semin-durr:64-64.t: His saying: {لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ}: its answer is omitted, i.e. "they would not have seen the punishment", or "they would have warded it off".

semin-durr:66-66.t: His saying: {فَعَمِيَتْ}: the generality read it light. Al-Aʿmash and Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read it with a ḍamma on the ʿayn and a doubled mīm [فعُمِّيَتْ]. The two readings of the Seven have preceded in Hūd. Ṭalḥa read «لا يَسَّاءَلُوْن» with a doubled sīn, by assimilating the tāʾ into the sīn, like the reading {تَسَّآءَلُونَ بِهِ والأرحام} [al-Nisāʾ: 1].

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying: {مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ الخيرة}: there are several views in it. The first: that «ما» is negating, so the pause is at «يَخْتار». The second: «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. "He chooses their choosing", the maṣdar standing in the place of the direct object, i.e. "what they choose".
The third: that it means الذي ("that which"), the referent pronoun being omitted, i.e. "that in which they had the choice", like His saying {وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الأمور} [al-Shūrā: 43], i.e. "of it".
Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted «كان» to be complete (tāmma) and «لهم الخِيَرَةُ» a resumptive clause. He said: "It seems sound to me that «ما» be an object if we assume the complete كان, i.e. Allah chooses everything that exists; and «لهم الخيرةُ» is resumptive, its meaning being an enumeration of the blessings upon them in Allah's choosing for them, had they accepted." Some placed in «كان» the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and recited:
3633 - أمِنْ سُمَيَّةَ دَمْعُ العين تَذْرِيْفُ ... لو كان ذا منك قبل اليوم معروفُ
(Is it because of Sumayya that the eye's tears are flowing? If only this had been known from you before today!)
[Translator's note: the verse number jumps from 3622 to 3633 in the source; kept as written.] Had «ذا» been its noun, he would have said «معروفاً». Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected that in the verse, saying: "Because the explanation of the [pronoun of the] matter and affair is not made by a clause in which something is omitted." I say: it seems he means that the preposition is attached to something omitted, and the pronoun of the matter is explained only by a clause with both its parts explicit. However, there is room for consideration in this if he meant it, because this preposition-phrase stands in the place of the khabar (predicate), and I do not think anyone would reject «هو السلطان في البلد» ("it is [the case that] the sultan is in the land") and «هي هندٌ في الدار» ("it is [the case that] Hind is in the house").
الخِيَرَة is from التخيير, like الطِّيَرَة from التَّطَيُّر; both are used as maṣdars. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ما كان لهم الخيرةُ» is an explanation of His saying «ويختار», because its meaning is 'and He chooses what He wills'; that is why the conjunction did not enter. The meaning is that the choice belongs to Allah the Exalted in His acts, and He knows best the aspects of wisdom in them; none of His creation may choose against Him." I say: people have continued to say that the pause at «يختار» and beginning with «ما» as negating is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunna — this is transmitted from a group such as Abū Jaʿfar and others — and that its being a relative connected to «يختار» without pausing on it is the doctrine of the Muʿtazila. Yet here is al-Zamakhsharī establishing it as negating and achieving his aim in his words, and it outwardly agrees with the words of Ahl al-Sunna, even though he does not intend that. And here is al-Ṭabarī, one of the great figures of Ahl al-Sunna, rejecting that [ما] be negating; he said: "Lest the meaning be that they had no choice in the past but have it in the future; and also, no negation has preceded." What Ibn Jarīr said is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās. Some said: "and He chooses for them whom He wills of the messengers", so «ما» on this view refers to rational beings.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» and «جَعَلَ» contend (tanāzuʿ) for «الليلَ», and the second was given governance. The object of «أَرَأَيْتُم» is the interrogative clause after it; the referent pronoun from it back to «الليل» is omitted, its implied form being "with light after it". The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. The working-out of this has passed in al-Anʿām, and this is its parallel.
And «سَرْمَداً» is a second object if the making is "rendering" (taṣyīr), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) if it is creating and bringing into being. السَّرْمَد is the perpetual, which does not cease. Ṭarafa said:
3624 - لَعَمْرُكَ ما أَمْريْ عليَّ بغُمَّةٍ ... نهاري ولا لَيْلي عَلَيَّ بسَرْمَدِ
(By your life, my affair is not obscure to me in my day, nor is my night perpetual upon me.)
The apparent view is that its mīm is radical and its pattern is فَعْلَل, like جَعْفَر. It has been said: it is additional, and its derivation is from السَّرْد, which is the succession of one thing upon another; except that the addition of the mīm in the middle and at the end is not regular, e.g. دُلامِص and زُرْقُم, from الدِّلاص and الزُّرْقَة.
His saying: {إلى يَوْمِ}: attached to «جَعَل», or to «سَرْمداً», or to something omitted as an adjective of «سَرْمَداً».

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying: {لِتَسْكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبتَغُواْ}: it is of the type of "folding and unfolding" (al-laff wa-l-nashr). From it:
3625 - كأنَّ قلوبَ الطيرِ رَطْباً ويابساً ... لدى وَكْرِها العُنَّابُ والحَشَفُ البالي
(As though the hearts of the birds, fresh and dry, by her nest were jujubes and worn-out dry dates.)

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying: {مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ}: «ما» is a relative meaning الذي; its ṣila (relative clause) is «إنَّ» and what falls within its scope, which is why it has kasra. Al-Akhfash the Younger reported from the Kufans the prohibition of making «إنَّ» a ṣila, and he considered that ugly on their part — meaning because it occurs in the Qurʾān.
His saying: {لَتَنُوءُ بالعصبة}: there are two views in it. The first: that the bāʾ is for transitivity like the hamza, and there is no inversion in the speech. The meaning is: the keys weigh down the strong band, as you say أَجَأْتُه and جِئْتُ به, أَذْهَبْتُه and ذَهَبْتُ به. The meaning of ناء بكذا is "he rose with it with difficulty". He said:
3626 - تَنُوْءُ بأُخْراها فَلأْياً قِيامُها ... وَتَمْشِي الهوينى عن قَريبٍ فَتَبْهَرُ
(She rises heavily with her hinder part, so her standing is with effort, and she walks gently a short way and becomes breathless.)
Abū Zayd said: "نُؤْتُ بالعَمَل, i.e. I rose [to the work]." He said:
3627 - إذا وَجَدْنا خَلَفاً بِئْسَ الخَلَفْ ... عبداً إذا ما ناء بالحِمْلِ وَقَفْ
(Then we found a successor — what a wretched successor! — a slave who, when he rises with a load, stops.)
Al-Zamakhsharī explained it as weighing down. He said: "One says: ناء به الحِمْلُ, [meaning] until it weighed him down and made him lean." On this the meaning fits, i.e. the keys weigh down the band.
The second: that there is inversion in the speech, and the original is "the band rises with the keys", i.e. carries them with effort. Abū ʿUbayd said this, like their saying «عَرَضْتُ الناقةَ على الحَوْضِ» ("I presented the she-camel to the trough"). The discussion of inversion has preceded, and that there are three doctrines regarding it.
Budayl ibn Maysara read «لَيَنُوْءُ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ and the masculine, because he took account of the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is "their load" or "their weight". It has been said: the pronoun in «مفاتِحَه» is for Qārūn, so the muḍāf acquired masculinity from the muḍāf ilayhi, like their saying «ذهبَتْ أهلُ اليمامةِ»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. He means: just as «أهلُ» acquired femininity, this acquired masculinity.
His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: there are several views in it: that it is governed by «تنوءُ» — al-Zamakhsharī said this; or by «بغى» — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh refuted both on the grounds that the meaning is not restricted to this time. Or by «آتيناه» — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; the Shaykh refuted it on the grounds that the giving was not at that time. Or by something omitted: Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as "he transgressed against them", and this ought to be refuted by what Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view was refuted with. Al-Ṭabarī estimated it as "remember", and the Shaykh estimated it as "he displayed exultation", which is fitting.
It was also read «الفارِحين»; ʿĪsā al-Ḥijāzī reported it.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {فِيمَآ آتَاكَ}: it may be attached to «ابْتَغِ», or to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "moving about in what He has given you". «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival) or means الذي.
His saying: {كَمَآ أَحْسَنَ}, i.e. "a good-doing like His good-doing to you".
His saying: {فِي الأرض}: it may be attached to «تَبْغِ», or to «الفساد», or to something omitted as a ḥāl, which is remote.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying: {على عِلْمٍ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative [pronoun] of «أُوتِيْتُه».
His saying: {عندي}: either an adverbial of «أُوْتِيْتُه» or an adjective of «العلم».
His saying: {مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ}: «مَنْ» is a relative or an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows]; it is in the position of the object of «أَهْلَكَ», and «مِنْ قبلِه» is attached to it. In «مِنَ القرون» the same is possible, and it may also be a ḥāl from «مَنْ هو أشدُّ».
His saying: {وَلاَ يُسْأَلُ}: this is the reading of the generality, in the passive, with the lower-dotted yāʾ and the verb in the nominative. Abū Jaʿfar read «ولا تُسْأَلْ» with the upper-dotted tāʾ and the jussive. Ibn Sīrīn and Abū al-ʿĀliya likewise, except that it is active, [the agent] being the one addressed. Ibn Abī Isḥāq said: "That is not permissible unless you put «المجرمين» in the accusative." The author of al-Lawāmiḥ said: "This is the apparent [requirement], except that nothing has reached me about it. If they left it in the nominative, it admits two views. The first: that «المجرمون» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. 'they are the criminals'. The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from the underlying [position] of the hāʾ and mīm in «ذُنوبهم», because they are nominative in position" — meaning that ذنوب is a maṣdar annexed to its agent. He said: "So «المجرمون» was construed on the underlying [position], as we have had in the reading {مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 26] with «بعوضة» in the genitive." He had explained it on the basis that the original was "by striking the parable of a gnat". This is much contrivance. Ibn Sīrīn and Abū al-ʿĀliya ought to have read only «المجرمين» with the yāʾ; its transmission was only omitted because it is obvious.

semin-durr:79-79.t: His saying: {فِي زِينَتِهِ}: either attached to «خَرَجَ», or to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «خَرَجَ».

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying: {وَيْلَكُمْ}: accusative by something omitted, i.e. "may Allah make your woe cling to you".
His saying: {وَلاَ يُلَقَّاهَآ}, i.e. this trait, which is renunciation of the world and desire for what is with Allah.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {فَخَسَفْنَا بِه وَبِدَارِه}: the well-known [reading] is kasra on the hāʾ of the pronoun in «به» and «بداره» because of the kasra of what precedes it. It was also read with a ḍamma on it; it has preceded that this is the original, and it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz.
His saying: {مِن فِئَةٍ}: it may be the noun of كان if it is incomplete (nāqiṣa), with «له» the khabar (predicate), or «يَنْصُرونه»; or it may be the agent if it is complete (tāmma), with «يَنْصُرونه» an adjective of «فِئَة», whose position is then judged genitive in form and nominative in meaning, because «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in it.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying: {وَيْكَأَنَّ الله}: and «ويْكَأنَّه»: there are several doctrines on it. Among them: that «وَيْ» is a word on its own, a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning "I marvel"; the kāf is for causation, and أنَّ with what falls within its scope is genitive by it, i.e. "I marvel, because the disbelievers do not prosper". It has been heard: «كما أنه لا يَعْلَمُ غفر اللهُ له» ("because he does not know, may Allah forgive him"). The analogy of this view is that one pauses on «وَيْ» alone, and al-Kisāʾī did that — except that it is transmitted from him that he believed the origin of the word to be وَيْلَكَ, as will come, and this contradicts his pause. Sībawayh recited:
3628 - وَيْ كأنْ مَنْ يكنْ له نَشَبٌ يُحْ ... بَبْ ومَنْ يَفْتَقِرْ يَعِشْ عيشَ ضُرِّ
(Ah! Whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.)
The second: some said that «كأنَّ» here is for comparison, except that its meaning has gone from it and it has become for statement and certainty. He recited:
3629 - كأنني حين أُمْسِي لا تُكَلِّمُني ... مُتَيَّمٌ يَشْتهي ما ليس موجودا
(It is as if I, when evening comes and she does not speak to me, am one enslaved by love, desiring what does not exist.)
This too fits pausing on «وَيْ».
The third: that «وَيْكَ» is a word on its own, the kāf a particle of address, and «أنَّ» governed by something omitted, i.e. "know that he does not prosper". Al-Akhfash said this. On it is his saying:
3630 - ألا وَيْكَ المَسَرَّةُ لا تَدُوْمُ ... ولا يَبْقى على البؤسِ النعيمُ
(Ah, look! Joy does not last, and ease does not remain in the face of misery.)
ʿAntara said:
3631 - ولقد شَفَى نفسي وأَبْرَأَ سُقْمَها ... قيلُ الفوارسِ وَيْكَ عنترَ أَقْدمِ
(What healed my soul and cured its sickness was the horsemen's saying, "Ah, ʿAntar, charge!")
On this the pause should be on «وَيْكَ», and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ did that.
The fourth: that its origin is وَيْلك, and it was shortened. Al-Kisāʾī, Yūnus and Abū Ḥātim went to this. They ought to pause on the kāf as Abū ʿAmr did. Those who held this adduced the two preceding verses as evidence, since it is possible that the original in them was وَيْلَكَ, shortened. In the Qurʾān it was written only as وَيْكأنَّ and ويْكَأنَّه, joined, in both places; the generality of readers followed the script, al-Kisāʾī paused on «وَيْ», and Abū ʿAmr on وَيْكَ. All this is in the pause of testing (waqf al-ikhtibār), not the pause of choice (waqf al-ikhtiyār), like parallels that have preceded.
The fifth: that «وَيْكأنَّ» as a whole is a single, simple, joined word meaning "have you not seen"; perhaps that is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ transmitted that it means "do you not see Allah's handiwork?". Ibn Qutayba reported that it means "mercy upon you" in the dialect of Ḥimyar.
His saying: {لولا أَن مَّنَّ}: al-Aʿmash read «لولا مَنَّ» with «أنْ» omitted, though it is intended, because this «لولا» is followed only by a mubtadaʾ (subject). From him also: «مَنُّ», with ḍamma on the nūn and the Divine Name in the genitive, which is clear.
His saying: {لَخَسَفَ}: Ḥafṣ [read] «لَخَسَفَ» in the active voice, i.e. Allah the Exalted; the rest in the passive, with «بنا» standing in place of the agent. ʿAbdallāh and Ṭalḥa [read] «لانْخُسِفَ بنا», i.e. the place. It has been said: «بنا» is what stands in place of the agent, as in your saying «انقُطِع بنا», and it is an expression . . . [Translator's note: there is a gap in the source here, marked by dots.] It has also been said: the agent is the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. "the sinking would have sunk", and this too is faulty expression. From ʿAbdallāh: «لَتُخُسِّفَ», with the upper-dotted tāʾ and a doubled sīn, in the passive, with «بنا» standing in its place.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying: {تِلْكَ الدار}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its adjective, and «نجعلها» is the khabar (predicate). It is possible that «الدارُ» is the khabar and «نَجْعَلُها» another khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial). The first is better.
His saying: {وَلاَ فَسَاداً}: He repeated «لا» to convey that each of them is independent in the verse, not the two combined.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ يُجْزَى الذين}: it is of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to denounce them.
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا كَانُواْ}, i.e. except the like of what they used to [do].

semin-durr:85-85.t:
His saying: {إلى مَعَادٍ}: its indefiniteness is for magnification, i.e. "a place of return — and what a place of return!", which is Mecca or Paradise.
His saying: {مَن جَآءَ بالهدى}: accusative by an implied [verb], i.e. "He knows", or by «أَعْلم» if we make it mean "knowing" (ʿālim) and give it its governance.

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً}: there are two views in it. The first: it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "but He had mercy on you with a mercy". The second: that it is conjoined (muttaṣil). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is speech construed according to the sense, as though it were said: 'The Book was not cast to you except as a mercy'." So it is an exception from the states, or from the object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu).
His saying: {وَلاَ يَصُدُّنَّكَ}: the generality read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the ṣād, from صَدَّه يَصُدُّه. It was also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ṣād, from أصَدَّه meaning صَدَّه; Abū Zayd reported it from Kalb. He said:
3632 - أناسٌ أَصَدُّوا الناسَ بالسيفِ عنهم ... صُدودَ السَّوافي عن أُنوفِ المَخارِمِ
(A people who turned others away from themselves with the sword, as the wind-blown sands turn away from the noses of the mountain passes.)
The original of يَصُدُّنَّك is يَصُدُّونَنَّك, and with it was done what was done in {لَّيَقُولُنَّ مَا يَحْبِسُهُ} [Hūd: 8]. [Translator's note: the source writes «يَصُدُّونك» / «يَصُدُّونَنَّك» here; translated as meaning the verse's word.]

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ وَجْهَهُ}: whoever holds that «شيء» ("thing") may be applied to the Creator, the Exalted — and that is the correct view — said: this is a conjoined exception (muttaṣil), and what is meant by the Face is the Essence; it only follows the custom of the Arabs in expressing the whole by its noblest part. Whoever does not apply it to Him also made it conjoined, and made the Face [mean] what is done for His sake, or the standing [one has] among people; or makes it disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "but He remains as He is and does not perish".
His saying: {تُرْجَعُونَ}: the generality read it in the passive; ʿĪsā in the active, and it is good.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {نَتْلُواْ}: its object may be omitted, indicated by its ṣifa (adjective), namely {مِن نَّبَإِ موسى}, the implied form being: "We recite to you something of the news of Moses". «مِنْ» may also be redundant (zāʾida), according to the view of al-Akhfash, i.e. "We recite to you the news of Moses."

His saying: {بالحق}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «نَتْلو» or from its object, i.e. "[We] being invested with the truth" or "[it] being invested with the truth"; or it is attached to «نَتْلو» itself, in the sense of "We recite it because of the truth". «لقوم» / is attached to the verb of reciting, i.e. "for the sake of these".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ}: this is what is recited, so it was brought in an emphasised resumptive clause.

His saying: {يَسْتَضْعِفُ}: three aspects are permitted in it. The first: that it is resumptive, an explanation of the state of the people whom he made into factions and classes. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جَعَل», i.e. "he made them so, while oppressing a group of them". The third: that it is a ṣifa (adjective) of «شِيَعاً».

His saying: {يُذَبِّحُ}: the three aspects are permitted in it: resumption, as an explanation of «يَسْتَضْعِفُ»; or a ḥāl from its fāʿil; or a second ṣifa of «طائفة». The majority read «يُذَبِّح» with doubling, for multiplicity. Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يَذْبَحُ», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the bāʾ, the imperfect of «ذَبَحَ», undoubled.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {وَنُرِيدُ}: there are two aspects in it. The more evident: that it is conjoined to His saying «إنَّ فرعونَ», a verbal clause conjoined to a nominal one, because both are an explanation of the news. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَسْتَضْعِفُ». There is weakness in this, both in terms of grammar and in terms of meaning. As for grammar, it is because it is an affirmative imperfect, which ought to be free of the wāw; and implying a mubtadaʾ (subject) before it, i.e. "while We intend", as in his saying:

3584 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . وأرْهَنُهُمْ مالِكاً
(…and I gave them Mālik as a pledge.)

is a strain for which there is no need. As for meaning, how can Pharaoh's oppression and Allah's intention of favour come together? For whenever Allah bestowed favour on them, Pharaoh's oppressing them would become impossible. This has been answered: since the favour of their deliverance from Pharaoh was swift and near in occurring, the intention of its occurring was treated as though it were simultaneous with their being oppressed.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {وَنُمَكِّنَ}: the majority read it so, without the lām of cause. Al-Aʿmash read «ولِنُمَكِّنَ», with the lām of cause, what it is attached to being omitted, i.e. "and in order that We might establish, We did that".

His saying: {وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ}: the two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يرى», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the rāʾ, the imperfect of «رَأى», attributed to Pharaoh and what is conjoined to him; for that reason they read [them] in the nominative. The rest read it with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the rāʾ, the imperfect of «أرى»; for that reason Pharaoh and what is conjoined to him are accusative as the first object, and «ما كانوا» is the second. «منهم» is attached to the verb of seeing or of showing, not to «يَحْذَرون», because what comes after a relative noun does not govern what comes before it. We have no necessity to say that latitude was allowed in it.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ}: it may be the explicative (mufassira) or the maṣdariyya (infinitival) «أن». ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid read it with kasra on the nūn, because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters; as though he dropped the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) irregularly, so two unvowelled letters met, and the first of them was given kasra.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِيَكُونَ}: the lām has the two well-known aspects: figurative causality — in the sense that, since that was the result and fruit of their action, it was likened to the motive for whose sake an agent does an act — or outcome (ṣayrūra). The majority read [«حَزَناً»] with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the zāy, which is the dialect of Quraysh; the two brothers read it with ḍamma and sukūn. They are two dialectal forms with one meaning, like «العُدْم» and «العَدَم».

His saying: {خَاطِئِينَ}: the majority read it with the hamza, taken from «الخَطأ», the opposite of what is right. It has been read with a yāʾ without hamza; it may be like the first but lightened, or it may be from «خطا يَخْطُو», i.e. "overstepped what is right".

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ}: there are two aspects in it. The more evident: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he is a comfort of the eye". The second — and it is very far-fetched — that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «لا تَقْتُلوه». It seems this proponent ought to have [the khabar] feminine and say «لا تقتلوها», except that since what is meant is masculine, that was allowed.

The majority of readers, exegetes and scholars pause on «ولَكَ». Ibn al-Anbārī transmitted, with his chain of transmission to Ibn ʿAbbās, that he paused on «لا», i.e. "he is a comfort of the eye for me only, and for you, no" — i.e. he is not a comfort of the eye for you — and then began with his saying «تَقْتُلوه». This ought not to be authentic from him: how could «تَقْتُلوه» remain without the nūn of the indicative and without anything requiring its omission? For that reason al-Farrāʾ said: "It is a grammatical error (laḥn)."

His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ}: a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause. Is it part of the speech of the Creator, the Exalted — which is the apparent sense — or part of the speech of Pharaoh's wife? As though, when she saw that his council had advised killing him, she said this to him, i.e. "you do what I tell you, and your people are not aware." Al-Zamakhsharī made the clause from His saying {وَقَالَتِ امرأة فِرْعَوْنَ} conjoined to «فالتقطه», and the clause from His saying {إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ} to «خاطئين» parenthetical between the two conjoined elements, / and made what the perceiving relates to of the same kind as the parenthetical clause, i.e. "they did not perceive that they were in error in picking him up". The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Whenever it is possible to take the speech according to its apparent sense without separation, that is better."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {فَارِغاً}: the khabar (predicate) of «أصبحَ», i.e. empty of reason, or of patience, or of grief — and this last is the most far-fetched; it is refuted by readings that contradict it. Faḍāla and al-Ḥasan read «فَزِعاً», with zāy, from «الفزع» (fright). Ibn ʿAbbās read «قَرِعاً», with qāf and with kasra on the rāʾ, and also with sukūn on it, from «قَرِعَ رأسُه», when his hair has receded. The meaning is: it was empty of everything, and everything receded from it, except the remembrance of Moses. It has also been said: the one with unvowelled rāʾ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «قَرَعَ يَقْرَعُ», i.e. it was struck. «فِرْغاً» has also been read, with kasra on the fāʾ, sukūn on the rāʾ and the dotted ghayn, i.e. "unavenged, in vain", as in his saying:

3585 - فإنْ يَكُ قَتْلى قد أُصيبَتْ نفوسُهُمْ ... فلَنْ يَذْهبُوا فَرْغاً بقَتْلِ حِبالِ
(If there are slain whose lives have been taken, they will not go unavenged for the killing of Ḥibāl.)

«فَرْغاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بِقَتْلِ». Al-Khalīl read «فُرُغاً», with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the rāʾ and the dotted ghayn, with this meaning.

His saying: {إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِي}: «إنْ» is either the lightened (mukhaffafa) one or the negating one; and the lām is either the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa) or in the sense of «إلاَّ».

His saying: {لولا أَن رَّبَطْنَا}: its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "she would have disclosed", as in His saying {وَهَمَّ بِهَا لولا أَن رَّأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ} [Yūsuf: 24]. {لِتَكُونَ مِنَ المؤمنين} is attached to «رَبَطْنا». The bāʾ in «به» is redundant (zāʾida) in the object, i.e. "to make him known". It has also been said: it is not redundant but causal, and the object is omitted, i.e. "to disclose the matter because of Moses", or "because of the revelation"; so the pronoun may refer to Moses or to the revelation.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {قُصِّيهِ}: i.e. follow his track, i.e. trace him.

His saying: {فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ}: i.e. she saw him. Qatāda read «بَصَرَتْ», with fatḥa on the ṣād, and ʿĪsā with kasra on it. Its meaning has been given in Ṭā Hā.

His saying: {عَن جُنُبٍ}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. "she watched him, concealing herself, being at a distance (ʿan junub)", or from the genitive noun, i.e. "[he being] far from her". The majority read «جُنُبٍ» with two ḍammas; it is a ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted noun, i.e. "from a distant place". Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "i.e. out of longing"; it is the dialect of Judhām, who say «جَنِبْتُ إليك», i.e. "I longed for you". Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the nūn; from Qatāda also with fatḥa on both. From al-Ḥasan «جُنْبِ», with ḍamma and sukūn; from Sālim «عن جانبٍ». They all have one meaning; similar are «الجَنَاب» and «الجَنابَة».

His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ}: a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause; what the perceiving relates to is omitted, i.e. "that she was tracing him", or "that he would be an enemy and a grief to them".

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {المراضع}: it has been said: it may be the plural of «مُرْضِع», which is the [nursing] woman. It has also been said: the plural of «مَرْضَع», with fatḥa on the mīm and the ḍād; and they allowed this to be a noun of place, i.e. the place of suckling, which is the breast, or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. the sucklings, meaning their kinds.

His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: i.e. before her tracing him.

His saying: {وَهُمْ لَهُ نَاصِحُونَ}: the apparent sense is that it is the pronoun of Moses; it has also been said: of Pharaoh. Among the charming things related: when she said that to them, they found her state suspicious and perceived that she was a relative of his; so she said: "I only meant: and they are sincere to the king"; and so she escaped from them. Ibn Jurayj said it. I say: this is called by the masters of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) "double-directed speech" (al-kalām al-muwajjah). Similar to it is when someone was asked, while among people some of whom loved ʿAlī rather than others, some Abū Bakr, some ʿUmar, and some ʿUthmān: "Which of them was dearest to the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one whose daughter was married to him."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تَحْزَنَ}: conjoined to «تَقَرَّ». The tear of joy is cool (qārra) and the tear of sorrow is hot. Abū Tammām said:

3586 - فأمَّا عيونُ العاشِقين فَأُسْخِنَتْ ... وأمَّا عيونُ الشامتينَ فَقَرَّتِ
(As for the eyes of the lovers, they were made hot [with tears]; as for the eyes of those who gloat, they were cooled [with delight].)

The detailed account of this has been given in Maryam.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {على حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), [either] from the fāʿil (agent): "being at a time of heedlessness", i.e. concealing himself; or from the object. Abū Ṭālib the reader read «على حينَ», with fatḥa on the nūn. The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] strained to account for it as treating the maṣdar like the verb, in that when the adverb is annexed to it, it may be made indeclinable on the fatḥa, as in his saying:

3587 - على حينَ عاتَبْتُ المشيب على الصِّبا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(At the time when I reproached grey hair over youth…)

«مِنْ أهلِها» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «غَفْلَة», i.e. issuing from its people.

His saying: {يَقْتَتِلاَنِ}: a ṣifa of «رجلين». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "a ḥāl from them". Sībawayh, though he allowed it from an indefinite noun / without restriction, others — and they are the majority — stipulate in it what would permit beginning [a sentence] with it. Nuʿaym ibn Maysara read «يَقَتِّلان», with assimilation: he transferred the fatḥa of the first tāʾ to the qāf and assimilated.

His saying: {هذا مِن شِيعَتِهِ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ṣifa of «رجلين», or of a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَقْتَتِلان»; the latter is far-fetched because [the description] is not transitory.

His saying «هذا، وهذا» is by way of recounting a past state, so it is as though the two were present. Al-Mubarrad said: "The Arabs point with «هذا» to the absent"; and he recited [the verse of] Jarīr:

3588 - هذا ابنُ عَمِّي في دمشقَ خليفةً ... لو شِئْتُ ساقَكُمُ إليَّ قَطِينا
(This is my cousin, caliph in Damascus; had I wished, he would have driven you to me as servants.)

His saying: {فاستغاثه}: this is the reading of the majority, from «الغَوْث», i.e. he sought his rescue and help. Sībawayh, Ibn Miqsam and al-Zaʿfarānī read it with the undotted ʿayn and the nūn [Translator's note: i.e. «فاستعانه»], from «الإِعانة» (assistance). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a misreading of the dots (taṣḥīf)." Ibn Jubāra, author of al-Kāmil, said: "The choice is the reading of Ibn Miqsam, because 'assistance' is more fitting in this context." I say: attributing taṣḥīf to these [scholars] is not praiseworthy, just as al-Hudhalī's [Translator's note: i.e. Ibn Jubāra's] excess in choosing the anomalous (shādhdh) is not praiseworthy.

His saying: {فَوَكَزَهُ}: i.e. he pushed him with his whole fist. The difference between «الوَكْز» and «اللَّكْز» is that the first is with the whole hand and the second with the fingertips; it has also been said: the reverse. «النَّكْز» is like «اللَّكْز». [The poet] said:

3589 - يا أَيُّها الجاهِلُ ذو التَّنَزِّي ... لا تُوْعِدَنِّي حَيَّةً بالنَّكْزِ
(O ignorant one, given to leaping about, do not threaten me — a snake — with a jab.)

Ibn Masʿūd read «فَلَكَزه» and «فَنَكَزَه», with lām and with nūn.

His saying: {فقضى}: i.e. Moses, or Allah the Exalted, or the pronoun of the act, i.e. the blow.

His saying: {مِنْ عَمَلِ}: [i.e.] from his whispering and his making things seem attractive; and the reference is to the killing that issued from him.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ}: the bāʾ may be for an oath, the response being an implied «لأَتُوْبَنَّ» ("I will surely repent"), explained by «فَلَنْ أكونَ». Or it may be attached to an omitted element, its meaning being causal, i.e. "protect me because of what You have bestowed on me", and on this follows his saying «فلن أكونَ ظَهيراً». «ما» is maṣdariyya, or in the sense of «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted. His saying «فلن» is a negation in its literal sense. Some claimed that it is a supplication, and that «لن» occurs in the place of «لا»; a group permitted that, adducing this verse and the poet's saying:

3590 - لَنْ تَزالُوا كذلِكُمْ ثُمَّ لا زِلْ ... تَ لهمْ خالِداً خُلُوْدَ الجبالِ
(May you never cease to be thus; and may you remain for them, enduring as the mountains endure.)

There is no proof in either, because negation is evident in both without supplying a supplication, even if [the supplication reading] is stronger in the verse.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {خَآئِفاً}: the apparent sense is that it is the khabar (predicate) of «أَصْبح», with «في المدينة» [attached] to it. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the khabar being «في المدينة». Taking «أصبحَ» as complete (tāmma), i.e. "entered upon the morning", is weak.

His saying: {يَتَرَقَّبُ}: it may be a second khabar, or a second ḥāl, or a badal (substitute) from the first ḥāl or from the first khabar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خائفاً», so that it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl. The object of «يترقَّبُ» is omitted, i.e. "he was watching for harm", or "for relief", or "for news: had it reached Pharaoh or not?"

His saying: {فَإِذَا الذي}: «إذا» is that of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and «الذي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Its khabar is either «إذا», with «يَسْتَصْرِخُه» a ḥāl; or «يَسْتَصْرِخُه», with «إذا» a supplementary element (faḍla) in its usual function. «بالأمس» is declinable (muʿrab), because whenever al- is prefixed to it or it is annexed, it is declined; and when it is bare of both, its state is known: the Ḥijāzīs make it indeclinable, and the Tamīmīs make it a diptote, as in his saying:

3591 - لقد رَأَيْتُ عَجَباً مُذْ أَمْسا ...
(I have seen a wonder since yesterday…)

although it is sometimes made indeclinable with al-, rarely, as in his saying:

3592 - وإنِّي حُبِسْتُ اليومَ والأمسِ قبلَه ... إلى الشمسِ حتى كادَتِ الشمسُ تَغْرُبُ
(I have been held today and yesterday before it, until the sun, until the sun almost set.)

It is transmitted with kasra on the sīn.

His saying: {قَالَ لَهُ موسى}: as for the pronoun, it has been said: it refers to the Israelite, because he was the cause of the first trouble; it has also been said: to the Copt.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ}: the apparent sense is that the two pronouns refer to Moses. It has also been said: to the Israelite, and the enemy is the Copt. The pronoun in «قال يا موسى» refers to the Israelite; as though he imagined roughness from Moses, and that is why he spoke thus; by this the news about him spread, whereas the killer had been in doubt.

The addition of «أنْ» is regular in two places. The first: after «لَمَّا», as here. The second: before «لو», when preceded by an oath, as in his saying:

3593 - أَمَا واللهِ أنْ وكنتُ حُرّاً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(By Allah, if I were free… [Translator's note: so in the text, «أنْ وكنتُ», apparently for «أنْ لو كنتُ»])

[and his saying]:

3594 - فَأُقْسِمُ أَنْ لو التَقَيْنَا وأنتُمُ ... لكان لنا يومٌ مِنْ الشَّرِّ مُظْلِمُ
(I swear that had we and you met, we would have had a day of evil, dark.)

The majority read «يَبْطِشُ» with kasra; Abū Jaʿfar read it with ḍamma.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {يسعى}: it may be a ṣifa (adjective) or a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the indefinite noun has been specified by the description in His saying {مِّنْ أَقْصَى المدينة}. If you make «مِنْ أَقْصَى» attached to «جاء», then «يَسْعَى» is a ṣifa and nothing else. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, basing it on the position of the majority; and it has been given / that Sībawayh permits that without condition. In the verse of Yā Sīn, «مْن أقصى» was put before «رجل» because he was not from its farthest part but only came from it; here He described him as being from its farthest part; they are two different men and two distinct stories.

His saying: {يَأْتَمِرُونَ}: i.e. «يَتَآمَرُوْنَ» in the sense of "they consult one another", as in the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab:

3595 - أرى الناسَ قد أَحْدَثُوا شِيْمَةً ... وفي كلِّ حادثةٍ يُؤْتَمَرْ
(I see that people have taken up a new habit: over every event there is consultation.)

From Ibn Qutayba: "they command one another"; he took it from the saying of the Exalted: {وَأْتَمِرُواْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ} [al-Ṭalāq: 6].

His saying: «لك»: it may be attached to what «الناصحين» indicates, i.e. "a sincere adviser to you, among the sincere advisers"; or to «الناصحين» itself, because of the latitude allowed with adverbials; or by way of clarification, i.e. "I mean: to you".

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {يَتَرَقَّبُ}: i.e. watching for His guidance and Allah's rescue of him.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {تَذُودَانِ}: a ṣifa (adjective) of «امرَأَتَيْنِ», not a second object, because «وَجَدَ» here is in the sense of «لَقِيَ» (met). «الذَّوْد» is driving away and repelling; [the poet] said:

3596 - فَقام يَذُوْدُ الناسَ عنها بسَيْفِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So he stood driving people away from it with his sword…)

It has also been said: [it means] held back. Its object is omitted, i.e. "they were keeping people away from their sheep", or "their sheep from jostling with the people". «مِنْ دونِهم» means: from a place lower than theirs.

His saying: {مَا خَطْبُكُمَا}: this has been given in Ṭā Hā. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "Its literal sense is: what is your «مَخْطُوب»? i.e. what is it you seek by keeping back? He called what is sought «خَطْب», just as what one is concerned with (al-mashʾūn) is called «شأن» in your saying «ما شَأْنُك؟»; one says «شَأَنْتُ شَأْنَه», i.e. I aimed at his aim." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Asking with «الخَطْب» is only about one afflicted or oppressed, or someone pitied, or someone who does something objectionable."

Shamir read «خِطْبُكما», with kasra, i.e. "who is your husband?" — i.e. "why are you watering and your husband does not water?" It is very anomalous.

His saying: {يُصْدِرَ}: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the dāl, from «صَدَرَ يَصْدُر», which is intransitive, i.e. "[until] they go back with their livestock". The rest read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the dāl, the imperfect of «أَصْدَرَ», made transitive by the hamza, with the object omitted, i.e. "they take their livestock back". The majority read the rāʾ of «الرِّعاء» with kasra; it is an irregular broken plural, because the regular plural of the adjective «فاعِل» with a weak final radical, like «قاضٍ», is «فُعَلَة», as in «قُضَاة» and «رُمَاة». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for «الرِّعاء» with kasra, it is regular, like «صِيام» and «قِيام»"; and it is not as he said, for the reason I have mentioned.

Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ. Abū al-Faḍl said: "It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of the adjective; for that reason singular and plural are the same in it"; or it is with omission of a muḍāf. It has also been read with ḍamma on it, and it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like «رُخَال» and «ثُناء».

Ibn Muṣarrif read «لا نُسْقي», with ḍamma on the nūn, from «أسقى». The difference between «سقى» and «أسقى» has been given in al-Naḥl.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {فسقى لَهُمَا}: its object is omitted, i.e. "[he watered] their sheep for their sake".

His saying: {لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ}: attached to «فقيرٌ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made «فقيرٌ» transitive with the lām because it was made to include the sense of 'asking' and 'seeking'. It may also mean: I am poor in respect of this world because of what You have sent down to me of the good of religion, namely deliverance from the wrongdoers."

I say: he means that «افْتَقَرَ» is made transitive with «مِنْ»; so either you make it a case of inclusion (taḍmīn), or you attach it to an omitted element. As for «أَنْزَلْتَ», it has been said: it is a past verb in its original sense, and by "the good" is meant the good of religion that preceded. It has also been said: it is in the sense of the future.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَاهُمَا}: Ibn Muḥayṣin read «فجاءَتْه حْداهما», dropping the hamza for lightness, irregularly, as in their saying «يا با فلان», and his saying:

3597 - يا با المُغيرة رُبَّ أَمْرٍ مُعْضِلٍ ... فَرَّجْتُه بالمَكْرِ مني والدَّها
(O Abū al-Mughīra, many a knotty matter have I resolved by my cunning and shrewdness.)

and «وَيْلُمِّه», i.e. «ويلٌ لأمِّه» ("woe to his mother"); [the poet] said:

3598 - وَيْلُمِّها خُلَّةً لو أنَّها صَدَقَتْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(What a friend she would be, if only she were true…)

«تَمْشي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «على استحياء» another ḥāl, either from «جاءَتْ» or from «تَمْشي».

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى}: it is related from Abū ʿAmr: «أُنْكِحك حدى», dropping the hamza of «إحدى»; this resembles the reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin «فجاءَتْه حْداهما». The doubling of the nūn of «هاتَيْن» has been given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

His saying: {على أَن تَأْجُرَنِي}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the fāʿil (agent) or from the object, i.e. "that being stipulated upon me", or "upon you". «تَأْجُرَني» is the imperfect of «أَجَرْتُه», "I was his hired man". Its second object is omitted, i.e. "that you hire yourself out to me", and «ثماني حِجَج» is an adverb (ẓarf) for it. The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted from al-Zamakhsharī that it is the second object. I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not make it a second object on this aspect; he made it a second object only on another aspect, while on this aspect he made it nothing but an adverb. Here is his text, so that it becomes clear to you. He said: "«تَأْجُرُني» is from «أَجَرْتُه», when you were his hired man, as you say «أَبَوْتُه» when you were his father; and «ثماني حِججٍ» is an adverb. Or it is from «آجَرْتُه» [thus], when you reward him; from this is the condolence / of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'May Allah reward you (ājarakum) and have mercy on you'; and «ثمانيَ حِجَجٍ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its meaning being the tending of eight years." So the Shaykh transmitted from him only the first of the two meanings mentioned for «تَأْجُرَني», and reported from him that he parsed «ثمانيَ حِجَج» as a mafʿūl bihi. How can that be sound or plausible? And look at al-Zamakhsharī, how he supplied a muḍāf so that the meaning would be sound with it, i.e. "the tending of eight years"; because it is the work on which the reward falls, not the time itself; so how can the reward be directed at time?

His saying: {فَمِنْ عِندِكَ}: it may be in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "then it is from you"; or of the accusative, i.e. "then you will have added them" or "bestowed them as a favour from yourself".

His saying: {أَنْ أَشُقَّ}: the object of «أُرِيْدُ». The literal sense of their saying «شَقَّ عليه» is: it split his thought into two halves, so that at one time he says "I can bear it" and at another "I cannot bear it". It is among the finest of figures.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); it points to what the two of them contracted upon, and the adverb is its khabar (predicate). «بين» was annexed to a singular because it is repeated by conjunction with the wāw. Had you said «المالُ بين زيدٍ فعمرٍو» ("the property is between Zayd, then ʿAmr"), it would not be permitted. As for his saying:

3599 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . بين الدَّخولِ فَحَوْمَلِ
(…between al-Dakhūl, then Ḥawmal.)

al-Aṣmaʿī used to reject it and transmit «وحَوْمَلِ», with the wāw. The correct version is with the fāʾ, and he [Translator's note: i.e. the one who accepts the fāʾ] interpreted the verse as: «الدَّخولِ وحَوْمَلِ» being two places, each of which comprises several places — as in your saying «داري بين مصرَ» ("my house is between [the parts of] Miṣr") — because it is the comprehensive place. The original is «ذلك بَيْنَنا» ("that is between us"), and it was split up by the conjunction.

His saying: {أَيَّمَا الأجلين}: «أيّ» is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb) is «فلا عُدْوانَ عليَّ». There are two views about this «ما». The better known: that it is redundant (zāʾida), as it is redundant with its sisters among the conditional particles. The second: that it is an indefinite noun, and «الأَجَلَيْن» is a badal (substitute) from it. Al-Ḥasan, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, read «أَيْما», with the yāʾ undoubled, as in his saying:

3600 - تَنَظَّرْتُ نَصْراً والسِّماكَيْنِ أَيْهُما ... عليَّ من الغَيْثِ اسْتَهَلَّتْ مواطِرُهْ
(I watched Naṣr and the two Simāks [stars], to see which of the two would pour its rains of bounty upon me.)

ʿAbd Allāh read «أَيَّ الأَجَلَيْنِ ما قَضَيْتُ», inserting «ما» between «الأجلين» and «قَضَيْتُ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the difference between the two positions of the redundant «ما» in the two readings? I say: in the widely transmitted reading it occurs as an emphasis of the vagueness of «أيّ», adding to its indefiniteness; in the anomalous one, as an emphasis of the fulfilling, as though he said: whichever of the two terms I am resolved to fulfil and have devoted my determination to."

Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Quṭayb read «عِدْوان». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: injustice is conceivable only in one of the two terms, the shorter of them, namely being required to complete the ten; so what is the meaning of injustice being related to both of them together? I say: its meaning is that, just as if I were required to do more than ten, [it would be injustice] without doubt, so likewise if I were required to do more than eight. He intended by that to establish the matter of choice, and that it is firm and settled, and that the two terms are equal: either this or this." Then he said: "It has also been said: its meaning is 'then I will not be a transgressor'; and it is a negation of injustice from himself, as in your saying 'there is no sin upon me and no liability'." The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His first answer is long-winded." I say: it seems the second pleased him; but al-Zamakhsharī did not approve the second, because it is not really an answer, for the question still remains; and so he transmitted it from someone else.

Al-Mubarrad said: "He knew that there would be no injustice upon him in the more complete of the two; but he joined them in order to make the first like the more complete in fulfilment."

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ}: Ḥamza read it with ḍamma on the jīm, ʿĀṣim with fatḥa, and the rest with kasra. They are dialectal forms for the stick at whose head there is fire; this is the well-known sense. Al-Sulamī said:

3601 - حمى حُبِّ هذي النارِ حُبُّ خليلتي ... وحُبُّ الغواني فهو دونَ الحُباحُبِ
وبُدِّلْتُ بعد المِسْكِ والبانِ شِقْوةً ... دخانَ الجُذا في رأسِ أشمطَ شاحبِ
(Love of my beloved and love of fair women have barred the love of this fire, so it is less than the glow-worm's flicker; and after musk and ben-oil I have been given, as misfortune, the smoke of firebrands on the head of a grey, haggard man.)

Some restricted it, saying: at whose head there is fire without flame. Ibn Muqbil said:

3602 - باتَتْ حواطِبُ ليلى يَلْتَمِسْنَ لها ... جَزْلَ الجُذا غَيرَ خَوَّارٍ ولا دَعِرِ
(Laylā's wood-gatherers spent the night seeking for her thick brands, neither brittle nor smoky-flaming.)

«الخَوَّار» is that which snaps; «الدَّعِر» is that which has flame. But there is usage that requires the presence of flame in it; the poet said:

3603 - وأَلْقَى على قَبْسٍ من النارِ جَذْوةً ... شديداً عليها حَمْيُها والتهابُها
(And he cast upon a flame of fire a brand, intense in its heat and blaze.)

It has also been said: «الجَذْوَة» is a thick stick, whether or not there is fire at its head; but what is meant here is only one at whose head there is fire.

His saying: {مِّنَ النار}: a ṣifa (adjective) of «جَذْوَةٍ». It cannot be attached to «آتِيْكُمْ» as «منها» is attached to it, because this fire is not the fire mentioned [before]. When an indefinite noun has preceded and the Arabs wish to repeat it, they repeat it as a pronoun or made definite by the al- of prior reference (al-ʿahdiyya); and both have been combined here.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {مِن شَاطِىءِ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. «الأَيْمن» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «الشاطىء» or of «الوادي». «الأَيمن» is from «اليُمْن», which is blessing, or from «اليمين», the counterpart of the left of the two limbs; on this, its meaning is relative to Moses, i.e. the one adjoining your right hand rather than your left. «الشاطىء» is the bank of a valley or river, i.e. its edge and side; likewise «الشَّطّ», «السِّيْف» and «الساحل», all with one meaning. The plural of «الشاطىء» / is «أشْطَاء»; al-Rāghib said this. «شاطَأْتُ فلاناً» means: I walked with him along the bank.

His saying: {فِي البقعة}: attached to «نُوْدِيَ», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الشاطىء». The majority read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ, which is the higher dialect. Maslama and al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read it with fatḥa; it is a dialectal form related by Abū Zayd, who said: "I heard them say: «هذه بَقْعَةٌ طيِّبةٌ» (this is a good spot)."

His saying: {مِنَ الشجرة}: this is a badal (substitute) from «شاطىء», with the governor repeated; it is a badal of inclusion (ishtimāl).

His saying: {أَن ياموسى}: «أنْ» is the explicative (mufassira) one. It has also been allowed to be the lightened (mukhaffafa) one, its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with the vocative clause explaining it; there is remoteness in this.

His saying: {إني أَنَا الله}: the majority read it with kasra, by implying the verb of saying, or by making the calling include its sense. It has been read with fatḥa, and there is a difficulty in this: if «أَنْ» is made explicative, «إِنِّي» must have kasra, as the resumption explaining with what the calling was; and if you make it the lightened one, «أَنِّي» must be rendered as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the maṣdar is a single word, while the pronoun of the matter is not explained by a single word. What this reading ought to be accounted for by is that «أَنْ» is explicative and «أني» is governed by an implied verb, its implied form being: «أنْ يا موسى اعلَمْ أنِّي أنا الله» ("O Moses, know that I am Allah").
